lines: Old Bertil: Orrin guards that well like someone would steal it. Who'd steal a hole?
Weaver Tamsa: I weave all day so I have something to do with my hands while Lise talks to her goats about me.
Weaver Tamsa: My threads stopped tangling by themselves. Strange how a Rift reaches so far.
Well-Keeper Orrin: Everyone here mocks me. The well is the only one who listens, and it just echoes.
Well-Keeper Orrin: The well water tastes of nothing again. That's how it should taste.
Goatherd Lise: My goats are smarter than Orrin. At least they leave the well when nothing happens.
Goatherd Lise: The goats climb up to the rim again. They hated the Rift more than I did.
Fiddler Brann: I play loud at night so nobody hears Tamsa gossip. It doesn't work. Nothing drowns her out.
Fiddler Brann: My fiddle stays in tune all night now. A small miracle, but mine.
Basket-Maker Ilse: Brann calls it music. The goats call it a warning.
Basket-Maker Ilse: The reeds by the fen stand straight again. Better baskets for everyone.
